Table 7: Comparison of spatial reasoning benchmarks across evaluation capabilities. ✓ marks a capability as an explicitly evaluated axis; ✗ marks absence or only incidental support. Multi-view: whether the benchmark evaluates multiple images, views, or viewpoint changes together as part of the task design. FoR: whether questions are anchored to the camera/viewer frame or to an oriented object’s intrinsic frame. FoR Mixing: whether a single query composes relations stated in different reference frames. Compositionality Type: Relation chains atomic spatial relations between specific objects; Skill composes heterogeneous capabilities such as recognition, localization, counting, or functional reasoning; 3D skill evaluates 3D spatial capabilities such as height, location, orientation, and multi-object reasoning; 6D relation evaluates spatial relations involving 3D position and orientation; Mental-model requires constructing an internal scene representation across partial views; Perspective evaluates viewpoint or frame-of-reference transformations; Perception evaluates low-level visual perception skills. Multi-hop / Chains: questions chain ≥2 atomic spatial relations between specific objects. Multi-hop / Controlled depth: hop count and topology are explicit, controlled axes. †FoREST is primarily a text/LLM frame-of-reference benchmark.
